track.title: Singapore mathematics
track.subject: Mathematics
track.description: An original K–12 planning sequence informed by Singapore MOE numeracy and mathematics syllabuses, connecting concrete experiences, diagrams, symbols and mathematical problem solving.
track.scopeNote: Editorial 36-week skeletons, not complete lessons, an official MOE programme, a commercial Singapore Math textbook series or a claim of standards certification. Library labels map K to a NEL preschool bridge, Grades 1–6 to Primary 1–6, Grades 7–10 to Secondary 1–4, and Grades 11–12 to JC1–2. These are navigation correspondences, not age, placement or qualification equivalences. This selected pathway uses standard primary Mathematics, G3 secondary Mathematics, elective G3 Additional Mathematics in Secondary 3–4, and elective H2 Mathematics in junior college. Foundation primary, G1/G2, H1, vocational and other pathways are valid alternatives not represented by these skeletons. Upper secondary and JC year splits and all pacing are editorial; schools can sequence combined-band content differently. Every SG- reference ID below is a local source locator, not an official MOE standard code. Activities are original outlines; formal assessment and qualification requirements require separate current guidance.

courses.title: Singapore mathematics — Kindergarten · NEL bridge
courses.scopeNote: Playful NEL preschool bridge; K is an editorial label. Observe conversation and action rather than require formal written arithmetic.
prerequisites: Participate in short shared play with support
Notice objects and communicate choices through speech, gesture or a home language
outcomes: Count and compare small collections
Describe repeating patterns and basic shapes
Explain simple part–whole arrangements
courses.nextStep: Build stable counting and number bonds before extending to Primary 1 numbers to 100.
courses.yearBridge: Sorting rules lead into stable counting and comparison. Repeating patterns and shape composition extend attention to structure; part–whole play and spatial directions then come together in a numeracy market.
courses.crossSubject: Retell a story with ordered events, positional words and counted props.
routines: Use objects, pictures and spoken explanations before symbols; accept pointing, building and oral responses.
Revisit counting, comparisons and pattern language during daily play; record observations across settings.

units.title: Notice, match and sort
units.focus: Discover useful attributes in familiar collections.
learning: Match objects by one shared attribute
Sort the same collection another way and explain the rule
activities: Sort buttons or classroom objects by a child-selected attribute
Make a mystery sorting tray for a partner to finish
evidence: Names or shows the attribute consistently
Accepts that one object can fit different sensible groups
units.bridge: A stable rule prepares children to order objects and identify a repeating unit.

units.title: Count collections and keep the total
units.focus: Coordinate number words, one-to-one matching and cardinality.
learning: Count at least ten objects reliably
Recognise that rearranging a set does not change its quantity
activities: Move each counted pebble onto a mat, then spread the pebbles apart
Match picture cards and numerals to small collections
evidence: Counts each object once and states the total
Keeps the total after rearrangement or recounts to check
units.bridge: Reliable collections make more, fewer and equal meaningful.

units.title: Compare and order
units.focus: Use matching and direct comparison before symbolic inequality.
learning: Compare two sets of up to ten objects
Order objects by length, height or size
activities: Pair toy passengers with seats and describe any unmatched objects
Order ribbons from shortest to longest with their ends aligned
evidence: Uses more, fewer and the same appropriately
Explains why a displaced ribbon must be realigned
units.bridge: Comparing wholes supports later comparisons of their parts.

units.title: Hear, see and extend patterns
units.focus: Recognise and describe a repeat, not just the next object.
learning: Extend and create repeating patterns
Describe the repeating unit using objects, sounds or actions
activities: Build a clap-tap-tap pattern and represent it with counters
Repair a bead pattern with a missing element
evidence: Repeats the entire unit consistently
Explains a missing item using the rule
units.bridge: Pattern language later supports number sequences and equal groups.

units.title: Shapes in many positions
units.focus: Recognise shape attributes despite orientation and size.
learning: Identify circles, squares, rectangles and triangles
Compose a new figure from familiar shapes
activities: Sort rotated and stretched shape cards and explain choices
Build a pretend playground from paper shapes
evidence: Uses sides or corners to justify a shape name
Names component shapes in a composite picture
units.bridge: Composition offers another way to think about parts making a whole.

units.title: Parts make a whole
units.focus: Explore number bonds within ten through play.
learning: Name two parts of a collection and its whole
Find more than one partition of a quantity
activities: Hide some of eight counters under a cup and reason about the missing part
Move a fixed collection between two toy homes
evidence: Reconstructs a hidden part with objects or a drawing
Shows that different partitions keep the whole unchanged
units.bridge: Number bonds become the foundation for addition and subtraction in P1.

units.title: Position, direction and sequence
units.focus: Describe locations and ordered actions precisely.
learning: Use positional and directional language
Arrange familiar events in a sensible sequence
activities: Guide a toy around a floor map using near, behind, left and right
Order picture cards for preparing a snack
evidence: A partner can follow the directions
Explains what happens before and after an event
units.bridge: Ordered language will support time, ordinal numbers and multi-step instructions.

units.title: A numeracy play market
units.focus: Bring counting, representation and comparison into one setting.
learning: Rote count to at least twenty while matching quantities within ten
Record small quantities with numerals, pictures or objects
activities: Build a class market with counted baskets and shape-based signs
Take turns explaining how many objects are needed to fill a partly full tray
evidence: Connects a numeral to its collection
Explains a part–whole or comparison decision without relying on layout
units.bridge: Start P1 with secure small quantities and extend place-value grouping gradually.

courses.title: Singapore mathematics — Primary 1
courses.scopeNote: Standard Primary 1 scope from the 2021 syllabus updated October 2025; the 36-week sequence is editorial.
prerequisites: Count at least ten objects and conserve a total
Describe parts of small collections and basic shapes
outcomes: Read, order and calculate with numbers to 100
Model addition, subtraction, equal groups and sharing
Use centimetres, clocks, shapes and picture graphs
courses.nextStep: Extend tens-and-ones reasoning to hundreds and develop multiplication tables in P2.
courses.yearBridge: Tens and ones give meaning to addition and subtraction; equal groups extend this reasoning. Measurement, clocks and money give quantities a context, and picture graphs bring counting and comparison together in a final plan.
courses.crossSubject: Read short mathematical stories and label drawings with quantities and units.
routines: Start with a short mental strategy and revisit an earlier topic each week.
Move between concrete materials, pictorial or bar models and symbolic work when each helps explain the structure.
Ask learners to estimate, explain the chosen representation and check by a second method; revisit errors after a delay.

units.title: Numbers to 100 and place value
units.focus: Make a ten a usable unit.
learning: Read and order numbers to 100 using tens and ones
Use ordinal numbers to tenth and describe number patterns
activities: Bundle craft sticks into tens to organise a stockroom
Arrange numbered tickets and explain missing terms
evidence: Represents a number with both bundles and numerals
Distinguishes an object count from its position
units.bridge: Tens and ones give meaning to written operations.

units.title: Addition and subtraction stories
units.focus: Connect parts, totals and differences to equations.
learning: Interpret joining, separating and comparison situations
Use addition to check subtraction within twenty
activities: Act out a changing collection, then draw it and write an equation
Compare two bead strings and label the difference
evidence: Matches an equation to a story rather than a keyword
Finds a missing part and checks the whole
units.bridge: Known bonds support making ten in larger calculations.

units.title: Calculate within 100
units.focus: Explain regrouping before practising a written algorithm.
learning: Add and subtract within 100 with tens-and-ones models
Add several one-digit numbers and choose useful pairs
activities: Trade ten ones for a ten while solving a supply problem
Compare counting-on, making-ten and column methods
evidence: Explains each exchange in a calculation
Uses a mental strategy for a two-digit number plus ones or tens
units.bridge: Flexible addition prepares repeated equal-group reasoning.

units.title: Equal groups and fair shares
units.focus: Introduce multiplication and division through meaning.
learning: Represent multiplication within forty
Share or group quantities within twenty
activities: Arrange identical seed packets into equal rows
Share counters among toy animals and draw each share
evidence: Connects a multiplication expression to equal groups
Distinguishes number of groups from objects per group
units.bridge: P2 formalises the inverse relationship and selected tables.

units.title: Length and shape construction
units.focus: Measure and compose with attention to units and boundaries.
learning: Measure and draw line segments to the nearest centimetre
Compose and describe figures using basic, half-circle and quarter-circle pieces
activities: Design a paper path from measured strips
Copy a tile picture on a dot grid and name its pieces
evidence: Aligns a ruler correctly and labels cm
Recognises a shape after rotation and separates parts from the whole figure
units.bridge: Measured lengths later support perimeter and area.

units.title: Clocks and daily duration
units.focus: Read clock structure in five-minute steps.
learning: Tell time to five minutes using am and pm
Describe durations of an hour or half an hour
activities: Build a movable clock and plan a pretend morning
Match two clock faces separated by thirty or sixty minutes
evidence: Reads minute and hour hands together
Explains why the hour hand moves between hour marks
units.bridge: P2 refines the five-minute structure to individual minutes.

units.title: Money and comparison problems
units.focus: Count amounts with different representations of value.
learning: Count cents to one dollar and dollars to one hundred
Use operations to solve simple money and comparison stories
activities: Make the same cent amount using different coin sets
Draw bars comparing the prices of two whole-dollar items
evidence: Separates coin count from total value
Labels the compared quantities and unknown difference
units.bridge: P2 combines dollars and cents in decimal money notation.

units.title: Picture graphs and a class plan
units.focus: Use counted information to answer and check a question.
learning: Read a picture graph and compare categories
Select a representation for a multi-topic whole-number problem
activities: Create a picture graph of pretend club supplies
Plan equal resource packs and check the plan with counters
evidence: Explains what one picture represents
Shows a calculation and checks it against the collection
units.bridge: Move to scaled pictures and hundreds while keeping the meaning of each unit visible.

courses.title: Singapore mathematics — Primary 2
courses.scopeNote: Standard Primary 2 scope from the 2021 syllabus updated October 2025; the 36-week sequence is editorial.
prerequisites: Use tens and ones to calculate within 100
Model equal groups and read a five-minute clock
outcomes: Calculate with numbers to 1000 and use tables of 2, 3, 4, 5 and 10
Represent and combine like fractions within a whole
Interpret metric measurements, solids and scaled pictures
courses.nextStep: Extend the remaining multiplication facts, equivalent fractions and area in P3.
courses.yearBridge: Hundreds extend place value, and table families organise equal groups. Fraction units develop alongside whole-number operations; money, clocks and metric measures require attention to units, while shapes and scaled pictures test how those units are represented.
courses.crossSubject: Write concise explanations of a measurement procedure and a graph comparison.
routines: Start with a short mental strategy and revisit an earlier topic each week.
Move between concrete materials, pictorial or bar models and symbolic work when each helps explain the structure.
Ask learners to estimate, explain the chosen representation and check by a second method; revisit errors after a delay.

units.title: Hundreds and three-digit calculations
units.focus: Extend the base-ten exchange system.
learning: Read and order numbers to 1000, continue number patterns, and distinguish odd and even numbers
Add and subtract three-digit numbers with justified regrouping
activities: Bundle sticks into hundreds and represent several arrangements
Audit a stock list using a written and mental calculation
evidence: Explains a zero in a place-value position
Checks subtraction by addition and an estimate
units.bridge: Place-value structure will extend unchanged to thousands.

units.title: Multiplication and division families
units.focus: Build the 2, 3, 4, 5 and 10 tables from structure.
learning: Use table facts and their related division facts
Distinguish sharing from grouping and use the division symbol
activities: Build arrays and derive a new fact from a known one
Create two different division stories for one fact family
evidence: Explains a fact using equal groups or an array
Checks a quotient with multiplication
units.bridge: Derived facts prepare the remaining tables in P3.

units.title: Fractions as equal parts
units.focus: Keep the whole and equal-sized parts explicit.
learning: Represent unit and like fractions with denominators at most twelve
Compare unit fractions and like fractions
activities: Fold equal paper strips into different numbers of parts
Sort fair and unfair sharing pictures and justify decisions
evidence: Names the whole before comparing fractions
Explains why more equal parts make each unit part smaller
units.bridge: P3 will rename fractions without changing their value.

units.title: Combine like fractions
units.focus: Count equal fractional units within one whole.
learning: Add and subtract like fractions within a whole
Explain numerator changes while the unit stays fixed
activities: Move fractional pieces on a strip to model a changing amount
Write a story for a missing fraction in a whole
evidence: Keeps the denominator consistent with the unit
Checks a subtraction by restoring the removed pieces
units.bridge: Conserving the unit prepares equivalent fractions and related denominators.

units.title: Dollars, cents and time
units.focus: Interpret two different systems of grouped units.
learning: Read, compare and convert dollar-and-cent amounts
Tell time to the minute and convert hours/minutes to minutes
activities: Run a pretend shop with amounts written in cents and decimal money
Build a schedule using clocks and labelled minute strips
evidence: Explains the value of each digit in a money amount
Uses sixty minutes per hour rather than one hundred
units.bridge: P3 operations with money and elapsed time depend on distinguishing these units.

units.title: Measure length, mass and liquid
units.focus: Choose a unit and instrument that fit the attribute.
learning: Measure using metres, grams, kilograms and litres
Compare and order measures of the same attribute
activities: Set up measuring stations for ribbon, sealed packets and water
Estimate first, measure, then discuss an unexpected result
evidence: Selects a suitable unit and records its abbreviation
Reads a simple scale without confusing length, mass and volume
units.bridge: P3 combines units and converts between larger and smaller units.

units.title: Shape patterns and solids
units.focus: Describe a repeat and a solid using its observable features.
learning: Extend patterns controlled by one or two attributes
Classify cubes, cuboids, cones, cylinders and spheres
activities: Create a pattern that varies orientation and size
Sort everyday containers and compare their surfaces
evidence: Identifies which attributes change and which stay fixed
Explains a classification without using colour as the defining feature
units.bridge: Later drawings and nets connect flat representations to these solids.

units.title: Scaled picture graphs and decisions
units.focus: Use equal groups to interpret one symbol standing for many.
learning: Read and compare quantities in scaled picture graphs
Choose operations for a multi-step class-supply problem
activities: Display pretend workshop attendance with one icon for several children
Plan supplies from the graph and compare two possible orders
evidence: Uses the graph key for totals and differences
Explains why a plan supplies enough without confusing icons with people
units.bridge: P3 carries the scale idea into bar graphs and the grouping idea into larger products.

courses.title: Singapore mathematics — Primary 3
courses.scopeNote: Standard Primary 3 scope from the 2021 syllabus updated October 2025; the 36-week sequence is editorial.
prerequisites: Calculate with three-digit numbers and selected multiplication tables
Read like fractions, money notation and metric units
outcomes: Use all multiplication tables and algorithms including remainders
Rename and combine related fractions
Distinguish area, perimeter, angle and measurement units
courses.nextStep: Extend to factors, mixed numbers, decimals and composite geometry in P4.
courses.yearBridge: Thousands and the remaining tables support larger calculations. Equivalent fractions make related-denominator operations possible; money and compound measures lead to elapsed time, then area, lines and angles provide new quantities to represent in bar graphs.
courses.crossSubject: Use labelled diagrams and time sequences to explain a practical procedure.
routines: Start with a short mental strategy and revisit an earlier topic each week.
Move between concrete materials, pictorial or bar models and symbolic work when each helps explain the structure.
Ask learners to estimate, explain the chosen representation and check by a second method; revisit errors after a delay.

units.title: Thousands and efficient addition
units.focus: Extend place value while keeping mental strategies active.
learning: Read and order numbers to 10000
Add and subtract up to four digits and calculate mentally with two-digit numbers
activities: Represent a library inventory with place-value disks
Compare compensation and column methods for a changed inventory
evidence: Explains regrouping through a zero
Selects and checks a reasonable mental strategy
units.bridge: P4 will use rounding and larger place values for estimation.

units.title: Complete the tables and divide with remainders
units.focus: Derive the 6, 7, 8 and 9 tables and interpret leftovers.
learning: Use multiplication/division facts from all tables
Multiply and divide up to three digits by one digit
activities: Split arrays into known facts to derive unfamiliar products
Pack counters into equal boxes and interpret the remainder
evidence: Connects each partial product to an array
Checks dividend = divisor × quotient + remainder
units.bridge: P4 extends the same algorithms to larger factors and dividends.

units.title: Equivalent and related fractions
units.focus: Rename equal quantities with a common fractional unit.
learning: Generate equivalent fractions and simplify them
Compare unlike fractions and add/subtract related fractions within one whole, with denominators at most twelve
activities: Overlay fraction strips to find matching boundaries
Solve a ribbon-sharing story with related denominators
evidence: Explains why renaming preserves value
Uses a common unit rather than adding denominators
units.bridge: P4 generalises to other denominator pairs and mixed numbers.

units.title: Money and compound measures
units.focus: Calculate quantities while respecting the unit system.
learning: Add and subtract money in decimal notation
Convert compound length, mass and liquid-volume measures to smaller units and back
activities: Reconcile a pretend shop receipt and change
Create labels for kilometre/metre, kilogram/gram and litre/millilitre supplies
evidence: Aligns dollar and cent units correctly
Explains a conversion using a unit relationship
units.bridge: P4 decimal place value will explain the notation already used for money.

units.title: Elapsed time and the 24-hour clock
units.focus: Use ordered time intervals across hour boundaries.
learning: Measure time in seconds
Find a start, finish or duration using 12- and 24-hour times
activities: Build a transport timeline with start and arrival labels
Compare two short activities timed in seconds
evidence: Partitions an interval accurately across an hour
Distinguishes 14:20 from a duration of fourteen hours twenty minutes
units.bridge: Rate problems later combine these durations with other quantities.

units.title: Area is coverage; perimeter is boundary
units.focus: Use arrays and length measures to build rectangle formulas.
learning: Measure area in square units, square centimetres and square metres
Find areas of rectangles and perimeters of rectilinear figures
activities: Make several rectangles using a fixed collection of square tiles
Trace and measure their boundaries and compare results
evidence: Uses square units for area and length units for perimeter
Shows that equal areas can have different perimeters
units.bridge: P4 uses these relationships to recover missing dimensions and decompose composites.

units.title: Angles and line relationships
units.focus: Investigate turns and line relationships with physical tools.
learning: Recognise angles smaller than, equal to or greater than a right angle
Identify and draw parallel and perpendicular lines
activities: Make a right-angle tester from folded paper
Draw a street plan with marked parallel and perpendicular routes
evidence: Checks an angle against a right angle rather than its arm length
Distinguishes perpendicular intersections from merely crossing lines
units.bridge: P4 measures angles numerically and uses rectangle properties.

units.title: Bar graphs and integrated planning
units.focus: Read scales and connect data to a defensible calculation.
learning: Read bar graphs with different scales
Combine grouping, measurement or money reasoning in a short plan
activities: Graph fictional garden harvest counts using two different scales
Plan equal produce bags, label leftovers and calculate a total price
evidence: Reads intervals even when not every value is labelled
Explains the remainder and checks the plan against the data
units.bridge: P4 extends graph interpretation to tables, lines and pie charts.

courses.title: Singapore mathematics — Primary 4
courses.scopeNote: Standard Primary 4 scope from the 2021 syllabus updated October 2025; the 36-week sequence is editorial.
prerequisites: Use four-digit arithmetic and all multiplication tables
Explain equivalent fractions, rectangle area and right angles
outcomes: Use factors and larger multiplication/division algorithms
Calculate with fractions and decimals within P4 scope
Interpret composite figures, nets, symmetry and data displays
courses.nextStep: Use decimal scaling, fraction multiplication, rates and triangle area in P5.
courses.yearBridge: Factors connect whole-number operations with fraction renaming. Decimal place value supports decimal arithmetic; composite rectangles and measured angles extend geometry, then nets, symmetry and data displays require careful interpretation of different representations.
courses.crossSubject: Compare a table and graph in a short informational text, describing the same data in words.
routines: Start with a short mental strategy and revisit an earlier topic each week.
Move between concrete materials, pictorial or bar models and symbolic work when each helps explain the structure.
Ask learners to estimate, explain the chosen representation and check by a second method; revisit errors after a delay.

units.title: Larger numbers, rounding and factors
units.focus: Connect place value, divisibility and estimation.
learning: Read and compare numbers to 100000 and round to tens, hundreds or thousands
Find factors, multiples, common factors and common multiples within syllabus limits
activities: Organise an imaginary museum collection using rounded inventories
Find possible equal rows for a collection and common meeting intervals
evidence: Explains the rounding boundary and uses the approximation symbol
Distinguishes a factor from a multiple with a numerical example
units.bridge: Factors and multiples provide the structure for fraction renaming.

units.title: Extend multiplication and division
units.focus: Keep the value of partial products visible.
learning: Multiply up to four digits by one digit and three digits by two digits
Divide up to four digits by one digit
activities: Compare an area model and a two-digit multiplication algorithm
Plan shipments with equal box capacities and interpret leftovers
evidence: Explains why the tens partial product shifts one place
Checks division with multiplication and a remainder
units.bridge: These algorithms will be reused with decimals and multi-step models.

units.title: Mixed numbers and fractions of sets
units.focus: Relate wholes, equal parts and groups of objects.
learning: Convert mixed numbers and improper fractions
Find a fraction of a set and add/subtract fractions with at most two denominators, each at most twelve
activities: Build lengths longer than one with fraction strips
Use counters and bars to compare fractional shares of a collection
evidence: Explains an improper fraction as a count of equal parts
Renames quantities into common units before combining them
units.bridge: P5 connects fractions to division and introduces fraction products.

units.title: Decimal place value
units.focus: Extend the base-ten system to thousandths.
learning: Read, compare and order decimals to three places
Connect decimals and fractions and round to a stated precision
activities: Partition a square model and place decimals on a number line
Sort close decimal values and explain trailing zeros
evidence: Compares values by place rather than digit count
Locates rounding boundaries and states the requested precision
units.bridge: Shared place values make decimal operations meaningful.

units.title: Calculate with decimals
units.focus: Use equal units and estimation to check decimal calculations.
learning: Add/subtract decimals up to two decimal places
Multiply/divide those decimals by a one-digit whole number and express whole-number quotients as decimals
activities: Share a measured ribbon and connect a diagram to long division
Compare exact and rounded totals for a pretend craft order
evidence: Explains decimal alignment by units
Checks the size of a product or quotient before rounding
units.bridge: P5 scales decimals by powers of ten and converts measurement units.

units.title: Composite rectangles and measured angles
units.focus: Use known properties to recover missing information.
learning: Find missing rectangle/square dimensions and composite area/perimeter
Measure, name and draw angles and use rectangle/square properties
activities: Design a stepped play space and mark internal decomposition lines
Draw a rectangle from dimensions and verify its angles
evidence: Avoids counting internal edges in the perimeter
Places the protractor centre and baseline correctly
units.bridge: P5 adds triangle area and reasoning with angle sums.

units.title: Symmetry, solids and nets
units.focus: Connect spatial objects to drawings and foldable surfaces.
learning: Complete a figure across a line of symmetry on a square grid
Interpret drawings of cubes, cuboids, cones, cylinders, prisms and pyramids; identify nets of cubes, cuboids, prisms and pyramids
activities: Predict which paper arrangements fold into a cube, then test
Draw a solid and its visible/hidden edges, and complete a reflected tile design
evidence: Pairs points at equal distances from the mirror line
Explains an overlapping or missing face in an invalid net
units.bridge: P5 uses spatial structure to count cubic units and calculate volume.

units.title: Tables, line graphs and pie charts
units.focus: Choose a display suited to the question.
learning: Complete tables and interpret line graphs and pie charts
Explain quantities, changes and category relationships in context
activities: Compare fictional water-use data in a table and line graph
Discuss a pie chart without assuming angles or percentages that are not given
evidence: Reads a scale and refers to a labelled category
Explains what the display supports and what it does not
units.bridge: P5 percentage and P6 averages add new ways to interpret familiar data.

courses.title: Singapore mathematics — Primary 5 · standard Mathematics
courses.scopeNote: Standard Primary 5 scope from the 2021 syllabus updated October 2025; the 36-week sequence is editorial.
prerequisites: Use decimal place value and operations by one-digit whole numbers
Rename fractions and decompose rectangular figures
outcomes: Multiply fractions and use ordered calculations
Apply percentages and rates with stated units
Find triangle area, rectangular volume and unknown angles
courses.nextStep: Develop fraction division, ratios, algebra and inverse percentage in P6.
courses.yearBridge: Large-number and decimal scaling establish unit reasoning. Brackets and fraction quotients lead into fraction products, percentages and rates; triangle area and cubic layers then support geometric measurements and angle deductions.
courses.crossSubject: Read a short science procedure and express its quantities as rates, volumes and measurements.
routines: Start with a short mental strategy and revisit an earlier topic each week.
Move between concrete materials, pictorial or bar models and symbolic work when each helps explain the structure.
Ask learners to estimate, explain the chosen representation and check by a second method; revisit errors after a delay.

units.title: Large numbers and decimal scaling
units.focus: Use powers of ten as changes of unit.
learning: Read and write numbers to ten million
Multiply/divide whole numbers and decimals by 10, 100, 1000 and their multiples; convert metric units
activities: Represent a large collection through grouped units
Build paired labels in metres/centimetres and litres/millilitres using decimal quantities
evidence: Explains scaling through place value rather than moving a decimal point mechanically
Keeps the physical quantity unchanged during a unit conversion
units.bridge: Unit conversion supports rates and volume calculations later this year.

units.title: Order of operations and mixed numbers
units.focus: Record multi-step relationships without losing their structure.
learning: Use brackets and order of operations without a calculator
Add and subtract mixed numbers and interpret a whole-number quotient as a fraction
activities: Write two expressions for a multi-stage packing plan
Share whole strips equally and record each share as a fraction and decimal
evidence: Explains how brackets change an expression
Regroups a whole when subtracting mixed numbers
units.bridge: Quotients and equal shares prepare fraction multiplication and division.

units.title: Fraction multiplication
units.focus: Interpret a product as equal groups or part of a quantity.
learning: Multiply proper and improper fractions and whole numbers
Multiply a mixed number by a whole number and explain whether a product grows or shrinks
activities: Overlay shaded rectangle models for a fraction of a fraction
Compare batches that use fractional amounts of material
evidence: Connects the model dimensions to numerator and denominator
Uses a magnitude check and simplifies without changing value
units.bridge: P6 reverses these multiplicative relationships in fraction division.

units.title: Percentages in familiar contexts
units.focus: Treat percent as a part measured against a whole of one hundred.
learning: Express a part as a percentage and find a percentage of a whole
Calculate a stated discount, GST or annual simple interest
activities: Build hundred-grid models for discounts on invented price tags
Compare two bills with explicitly supplied tax and interest rates
evidence: Identifies the correct whole in each calculation
Shows the percentage amount separately from the final total
units.bridge: P6 works backward from a percentage part and analyses percentage change.

units.title: Rates and unit reasoning
units.focus: Express one quantity for each unit of another.
learning: Find a rate, total amount or number of units from the other two
Track measurement units through a rate calculation
activities: Compare filling machines with different output and time records
Plan supplies using price per item and volume per container
evidence: Labels the per-unit quantity and distinguishes it from the total
Explains why the chosen multiplication or division matches the units
units.bridge: P6 ratios compare like quantities; S1 extends rates to speed.

units.title: Triangle area and composite regions
units.focus: Relate a triangle to a rectangle with the same base and height.
learning: Identify a perpendicular height even when it lies outside a triangle
Find triangle and composite areas
activities: Rearrange cut triangles into equal-area rectangles
Design a sign assembled from rectangles and triangles
evidence: Uses a perpendicular height rather than a sloping side
Accounts for each piece exactly once with square units
units.bridge: P6 adds circular pieces to composite-area reasoning.

units.title: Cubes, cuboids and liquid volume
units.focus: Build volume as layers of equal cubic units.
learning: Find cube/cuboid volume and draw solids on an isometric grid
Relate rectangular-tank volume to litres, millilitres and cubic centimetres
activities: Build and sketch equal-volume cuboids from unit cubes
Predict the water volume in a partly filled rectangular container
evidence: Explains the product of length, width and height using layers
Uses cubic units and the correct liquid-volume relationship
units.bridge: P6 recovers missing dimensions and base areas from a given volume.

units.title: Angles, triangles and quadrilaterals
units.focus: Derive unknown angles from stated geometric relationships.
learning: Use straight-line, point and vertically opposite angle relationships
Use triangle sums and properties of parallelograms, rhombuses and trapeziums
activities: Sort quadrilaterals by their properties, including rotated examples
Create a composite diagram with one unknown angle and explain a solution without adding lines
evidence: Names the property supporting each deduction
Does not assume a figure is to scale or use unmarked equalities
units.bridge: P6 combines these angle relationships; S1 generalises them to polygons.

courses.title: Singapore mathematics — Primary 6 · standard Mathematics
courses.scopeNote: Standard Primary 6 scope from the 2021 syllabus updated October 2025; the 36-week sequence is editorial.
prerequisites: Multiply fractions and use percentages and unit rates
Find triangle area and cuboid volume; explain basic angle relationships
outcomes: Divide proper fractions and interpret ratios
Represent relationships with simple algebra and reverse percentages
Use circle measures, inverse volume calculations and averages
courses.nextStep: Enter G3 Secondary 1 through signed numbers, general algebra and formal proportional reasoning.
courses.yearBridge: Fraction division reverses familiar products; ratios organise common units and reverse percentages recover missing wholes. Bar models become algebraic expressions, then circle, volume, angle and average problems test whether the learner can choose and check a suitable representation.
courses.crossSubject: Translate a multi-step written problem into a labelled representation, then write a conclusion answering its exact question.
routines: Start with a short mental strategy and revisit an earlier topic each week.
Move between concrete materials, pictorial or bar models and symbolic work when each helps explain the structure.
Ask learners to estimate, explain the chosen representation and check by a second method; revisit errors after a delay.

units.title: Division with fractions
units.focus: Use equal sharing and measurement to explain division.
learning: Divide a proper fraction by a whole number
Divide a whole number or proper fraction by a proper fraction without a calculator
activities: Partition a fractional strip among equal recipients
Count how many fractional scoops fit a given amount
evidence: Explains a quotient with a diagram before using a reciprocal rule
Checks division by multiplication and interprets the result
units.bridge: Fraction fluency supports rational-number operations in secondary school.

units.title: Ratio and common units
units.focus: Compare quantities through a shared multiplicative unit.
learning: Represent and simplify two- and three-part whole-number ratios
Divide a quantity in a ratio and connect ratio with fractions of the whole
activities: Use bars to allocate an invented club supply budget
Compare a part-to-part ratio and the corresponding part-to-whole fraction
evidence: Labels what each ratio term counts
Finds one ratio unit and verifies that the parts sum to the total
units.bridge: S1 extends ratios to fractional and decimal quantities.

units.title: Reverse percentages and change
units.focus: Keep the reference whole visible when working backward.
learning: Find a whole from a part and its percentage
Calculate percentage increase/decrease and distinguish original from final amounts
activities: Reconstruct a price before a stated discount
Compare two successive changes using bars and numerical examples
evidence: Uses the original amount as the change reference
Explains why equal percentage increase and decrease need not cancel
units.bridge: S1 consolidates reverse percentages and distinguishes percentage points.

units.title: From bars to algebra
units.focus: Give a symbol to a repeated unknown quantity.
learning: Write, simplify and evaluate simple linear expressions without brackets
Solve simple linear equations with whole-number coefficients
activities: Label matching bar segments with one letter
Compare an arithmetic bar-model solution and a symbolic solution to a packing problem
evidence: Distinguishes an expression from an equation
Substitutes a solution into the original equation to check it
units.bridge: S1 introduces signed coefficients, brackets, formulas and linear graphs.

units.title: Circles and composite measures
units.focus: Relate radius, diameter, circumference and area.
learning: Find circle area and circumference
Find areas and perimeters involving semicircles, quarter circles and earlier polygons
activities: Measure several circular lids and compare circumference with diameter
Design a curved garden border and mark which edges belong to its boundary
evidence: Uses radius and diameter correctly
Separates straight boundary segments from arcs and uses square units for area
units.bridge: S1 extends composite measures and later secondary work generalises circular sectors.

units.title: Solve volume problems backward
units.focus: Use multiplicative structure to recover missing dimensions.
learning: Find a cuboid dimension or base area from its volume
Find a cube edge from volume and use square/cube-root notation where needed
activities: Build possible tanks for a fixed volume and base area
Compare a cubic container with a rectangular container of equal volume
evidence: Connects division to the missing factor
Checks a recovered dimension by rebuilding the original volume
units.bridge: S1 extends root reasoning and volume to prisms and cylinders.

units.title: Composite angles and averages
units.focus: Use conserved totals in geometric and numerical settings.
learning: Find unknown angles in composite figures without adding lines
Relate average, total value and number of data values
activities: Explain an angle puzzle using marked triangle and quadrilateral properties
Redistribute counters to model equal shares and reconstruct a missing data value
evidence: Gives a reason for each angle deduction
Distinguishes an average from a sum and checks the reconstructed total
units.bridge: Secondary geometry formalises proof; statistics compares several measures of centre.

units.title: Choose, solve and explain
units.focus: Integrate representations while keeping each quantity defined.
learning: Choose bars, tables or equations for an unfamiliar multi-step situation
Evaluate whether a result meets all stated conditions
activities: Plan a fictional school event using ratio allocations, prices and average attendance
Revise a solution after a partner changes one constraint
evidence: Justifies the chosen model and checks units and totals
Explains which conclusions change and which remain valid
units.bridge: Begin S1 by revisiting these models and extending the number system beyond positive quantities.

courses.title: Singapore mathematics — Secondary 1 · G3 Mathematics
courses.scopeNote: G3 Secondary 1 Mathematics scope; the 36-week sequence is editorial.
prerequisites: Use P6 fractions, ratios, percentages and simple equations
Interpret geometric measures and numerical data
outcomes: Calculate with signed and rational numbers
Model relationships with expressions, equations and linear graphs
Use polygon geometry, mensuration and critical data displays
courses.nextStep: Develop quadratics, systems, similarity, trigonometry and probability in Secondary 2.
courses.yearBridge: Signed numbers and proportional comparisons support general expressions, equations and linear graphs. Angle deductions and dimensional measurement extend geometric reasoning; data critique and an integrated proposal then require learners to choose models and explain their limits.
courses.crossSubject: Read quantitative claims in an informational text and explain how units, graph scales and reference quantities affect meaning.
routines: Retrieve earlier number and algebra ideas each week and connect new work to diagrams and graphs.
Compare at least two representations or methods, then justify assumptions, restrictions and units.
Use technology to investigate and check; retain exact reasoning and explain what a numerical or graphical result can establish.

units.title: Number structure and signed quantities
units.focus: Extend whole-number structure to the real-number line.
learning: Use prime factorisation to find HCF, LCM, squares, cubes and roots
Calculate with integers and rational numbers and order real numbers
Round to a specified number of decimal places or significant figures and estimate calculation results
activities: Build factor trees and compare packing/repetition situations
Represent changes of elevation with signed number lines
Compare exact, rounded and calculator results for a set of measured quantities and explain an implausible display
evidence: Selects HCF or LCM from the situation
Explains signs and operation order rather than applying an unexplained rule
Distinguishes decimal-place accuracy from significant-figure accuracy and uses estimation to check a calculator result
units.bridge: Algebra will use the same signed operations on coefficients.

units.title: Ratio, percentage, rate and speed
units.focus: Model multiplicative comparisons with a defined reference quantity.
learning: Simplify ratios involving rational numbers and solve reverse-percentage problems
Use average rate/speed, convert km/h and m/s, and distinguish percentage points
activities: Compare two invented travel plans with different stops and distances
Analyse a percentage claim using a bar model and explicit reference total
evidence: Computes average speed from total distance and total time
Explains why a percentage-point difference is not the same as relative percentage change
units.bridge: S2 expands proportional reasoning to direct and inverse variation.

units.title: Expressions, patterns and formulas
units.focus: Express a relationship that applies to many cases.
learning: Generate an nth-term expression from a pattern
Expand linear brackets, collect like terms and extract common factors
activities: Build growing tile patterns and compare counting methods
Translate a rental-fee rule into an expression and evaluate several inputs
evidence: Explains what each coefficient or constant counts
Checks equivalent expressions at values and by structure
units.bridge: S2 extends expansion to products of expressions and quadratic factorisation.

units.title: Linear equations and graphs
units.focus: Connect balance, coordinates and constant rate of change.
learning: Solve linear and reducible simple fractional equations
Plot linear functions and interpret positive/negative gradient
activities: Compare two ways of solving a balance problem
Graph a changing water level and connect its table, equation and gradient
evidence: Checks a solution in the original equation and respects a denominator restriction
Explains rise over run with units
units.bridge: S2 studies intersections as simultaneous equations and contrasts quadratic change.

units.title: Angles, polygons and constructions
units.focus: Use geometric properties as reasons rather than visual guesses.
learning: Use parallel-line angles and interior/exterior polygon sums
Classify quadrilaterals and construct figures with appropriate tools
activities: Triangulate convex polygons to explain their interior-angle totals
Construct a design from angle and side constraints and annotate its properties
evidence: Links each unknown angle to a named property
Distinguishes a measured construction from a proof of its properties
units.bridge: S2 studies when two figures are congruent or similar.

units.title: Area, surface area and volume
units.focus: Decompose figures and track linear, square and cubic units.
learning: Find areas of parallelograms/trapeziums and composite figures
Find prism/cylinder surface area and volume, including unit conversions
activities: Derive a trapezium area formula using duplicate paper shapes
Compare container designs with equal volume but different surface areas
evidence: Explains the base and perpendicular height
Converts square/cubic units using the dimensional scale factor
units.bridge: S2 introduces pyramids, cones and spheres.

units.title: Represent and critique data
units.focus: Connect a display choice to the question it can answer.
learning: Collect, classify and tabulate a small data set
Compare tables, bar/picture/line graphs and pie charts and identify misleading displays
activities: Show one fictional data set with two different vertical-axis choices
Design an appropriate display for a category comparison or time trend
evidence: Explains what a graph obscures or exaggerates
Makes a claim supported by quantities and labels
units.bridge: S2 moves from displays to distributions and measures of centre.

units.title: A mathematical proposal
units.focus: Coordinate a model across number, algebra and geometry.
learning: State assumptions and select relevant information
Check a proposal against several numerical constraints
activities: Plan a fictional excursion with travel rates, costs and a venue floor plan
Compare the proposal with a partner plan after one assumption changes
evidence: Provides a labelled equation or diagram for each key relationship
Reports a feasible result and explains a limitation of the model
units.bridge: Carry algebraic fluency and unit reasoning into S2 systems and proportional models.

courses.title: Singapore mathematics — Secondary 2 · G3 Mathematics
courses.scopeNote: G3 Secondary 2 Mathematics scope; the 36-week sequence is editorial.
prerequisites: Operate with signed rational numbers and simplify linear expressions
Solve linear equations and interpret gradient and polygon geometry
outcomes: Factor quadratics and solve linear systems
Use similarity, right-triangle trigonometry and solid geometry
Compare distributions and calculate simple-event probabilities
courses.nextStep: Continue into the selected G3 plus Additional Mathematics upper-secondary pathway.
courses.yearBridge: Algebraic products and fractions support simultaneous equations and quadratic functions. Proportion leads to similarity and trigonometry, which support solid geometry; distribution and probability work add evidence for the final design investigation.
courses.crossSubject: Write a short mathematical argument that states a claim, evidence, restrictions and conclusion.
routines: Retrieve earlier number and algebra ideas each week and connect new work to diagrams and graphs.
Compare at least two representations or methods, then justify assumptions, restrictions and units.
Use technology to investigate and check; retain exact reasoning and explain what a numerical or graphical result can establish.

units.title: Algebraic products and fractions
units.focus: Preserve equivalence while changing form.
learning: Expand products and factor quadratic expressions using identities and grouping
Operate with simple algebraic fractions and change the subject of a formula
activities: Use algebra tiles to compare expanded and factored forms
Analyse two claimed simplifications and find an invalid cancellation
evidence: Checks factorisation by expansion
States excluded denominator values and preserves them after cancellation
units.bridge: These forms support quadratic solving and advanced functions.

units.title: Systems and linear inequalities
units.focus: Interpret a simultaneous solution as satisfying every condition.
learning: Solve two linear equations by substitution, elimination and graphs
Solve simple linear inequalities and display their solution sets
activities: Model two unknown ticket prices from two purchase totals
Compare an exact intersection with a graphical estimate and a feasible price interval
evidence: Substitutes into both original equations
Reverses an inequality when multiplying or dividing by a negative number
units.bridge: Upper secondary extends inequalities and introduces nonlinear intersections.

units.title: Quadratic graphs and equations
units.focus: Connect roots, symmetry and the shape of a parabola.
learning: Graph quadratic functions and identify maximum/minimum points
Solve quadratic equations by factorisation
activities: Build a table for a rectangular-area model with fixed perimeter
Compare an equation with its factored expression and graph
evidence: Uses the zero-product relationship correctly
Distinguishes roots, a vertex and a maximum value
units.bridge: S3 adds completing the square, discriminants and the quadratic formula.

units.title: Proportion, scales and similarity
units.focus: Distinguish additive changes from multiplicative scale.
learning: Model direct and inverse proportion and interpret map scales
Use corresponding angles/sides in congruent and similar figures
activities: Compare two scale maps and a fixed-work completion table
Enlarge a design and explain the correspondence between its sides
evidence: Identifies a constant ratio or product and its units
Matches corresponding sides before setting up a proportion
units.bridge: Upper secondary extends length scale to area and volume scale.

units.title: Right triangles and trigonometry
units.focus: Use triangle structure to find inaccessible lengths.
learning: Apply Pythagoras and its converse
Use sine, cosine and tangent for acute angles in right triangles
activities: Derive a square-area relationship with a rearrangement
Estimate a height from an invented survey diagram and compare methods
evidence: Identifies the hypotenuse relative to the right angle
Selects a trigonometric ratio from known and unknown sides and checks the angle unit
units.bridge: S3 extends trigonometry to non-right triangles and bearings.

units.title: Pyramids, cones and spheres
units.focus: Interpret solid formulas through dimensions and surface pieces.
learning: Calculate surface areas and volumes of pyramids, cones and spheres
Distinguish slant height from perpendicular height
activities: Compare model packaging for a specified volume
Sketch a cone net and label its surface and height information
evidence: Uses slant height for the appropriate surface calculation
Reports square or cubic units and a sensible magnitude
units.bridge: Upper secondary similarity compares related solids through scale factors.

units.title: Distributions, centre and chance
units.focus: Summarise variation and count equally likely outcomes.
learning: Interpret dot plots, histograms and stem-and-leaf diagrams, calculate suitable averages and calculate a mean for grouped data
Calculate simple-event probabilities from a complete sample space
activities: Compare two fictional travel-time sets with an outlier
Design a simple spinner game and list outcomes before calculating chance
Organise fictional travel times in a frequency table and compare its grouped mean with the mean of the original values
evidence: Explains when mean or median better describes a set
Distinguishes observed frequency from a theoretical probability
Weights each value or class midpoint by its frequency and identifies when the grouped mean is an estimate
units.bridge: S4 adds measures of spread and combined events.

units.title: Test a design with mathematics
units.focus: Combine models and explain the limits of a conclusion.
learning: Use equations, scale or data to evaluate a constrained design
Check and revise a solution after examining evidence
activities: Propose a small exhibition layout with scaled models and costs
Compare visitor-time data for two layouts and defend a summary measure
evidence: Connects each representation to the same quantities
Identifies one assumption or missing measurement that affects the recommendation
units.bridge: Before S3, revisit factorisation, fractional algebra and trigonometric meaning; these support the elective advanced sequence.

courses.title: Singapore mathematics — Secondary 3 · G3 + Additional Mathematics
courses.scopeNote: Selected advanced pathway combining G3 Mathematics and elective Additional Mathematics. Content is published for Secondary 3–4 together; this split is editorial and needs teaching time for both subjects.
prerequisites: Factor quadratics and operate with algebraic fractions
Use linear systems, similarity and right-triangle trigonometry
outcomes: Analyse quadratic, polynomial, exponential and trigonometric relationships
Use circle, coordinate and triangle geometry
Explain exact forms, solution restrictions and mathematical models
courses.nextStep: Develop calculus while consolidating G3 vectors, matrices, statistics and probability in Secondary 4.
courses.yearBridge: Indices and exact algebra support quadratic and polynomial analysis. Exponential and logarithmic models extend the available function families; coordinate geometry, general triangles and trigonometric identities then provide multiple ways to explain the final modelling investigation.
courses.crossSubject: Compare a scientific model with a verbal description, making the input, output and domain explicit.
routines: Retrieve earlier number and algebra ideas each week and connect new work to diagrams and graphs.
Compare at least two representations or methods, then justify assumptions, restrictions and units.
Use technology to investigate and check; retain exact reasoning and explain what a numerical or graphical result can establish.

units.title: Indices, standard form and surds
units.focus: Extend exact calculation to powers and irrational quantities.
learning: Use zero, negative and fractional indices and standard form
Simplify surds, rationalise denominators and solve simple surd equations
activities: Compare quantities over several orders of magnitude
Trace a surd equation through squaring and check all candidates
evidence: Explains an exponent law using equivalent expressions
Rejects an extraneous candidate in the original equation
units.bridge: Exact algebra supports quadratic roots and exponential models.

units.title: Quadratics and nonlinear intersections
units.focus: Choose a form that exposes the needed property.
learning: Complete the square, use the quadratic formula and interpret the discriminant
Solve quadratic inequalities and systems with one linear equation
Solve simultaneous linear inequalities and fractional equations reducible to quadratics, retaining restrictions
activities: Model a rectangular enclosure and compare factored, expanded and completed-square forms
Vary a line and predict the number of intersections with a parabola
evidence: Connects a discriminant sign to real intersections
Uses a sign chart or graph to justify an interval solution
units.bridge: Stationary-value reasoning here will later be generalised by derivatives.

units.title: Polynomials, partial fractions and binomial expansion
units.focus: Use structure to make complicated expressions manageable.
learning: Use polynomial division, remainder/factor theorems and sum/difference of cubes
Decompose syllabus-form rational expressions and use the positive-integer binomial theorem
activities: Find a missing polynomial coefficient from an imposed root
Compare a binomial coefficient calculation with successive expansions and reconstruct a partial-fraction identity
evidence: Checks a factor by substitution and multiplication
Matches coefficients and preserves denominator restrictions
units.bridge: These forms become useful integration tools in the advanced pathway.

units.title: Exponential and logarithmic models
units.focus: Treat a logarithm as the inverse question to exponentiation.
learning: Solve simple exponential/logarithmic equations using laws and change of base
Interpret growth/decay and compound-interest models and linearise a power or exponential relationship
activities: Build a model for an invented culture with a fixed growth factor
Plot transformed data to estimate constants and test a prediction
evidence: States domain restrictions before combining logarithms
Interprets parameters and checks a solution in the original model
units.bridge: H2 will place these examples within a general framework of functions and inverses.

units.title: Coordinates, circles and geometric proof
units.focus: Join algebraic descriptions to geometric reasons.
learning: Use line equations, midpoint, distance and parallel/perpendicular conditions
Use circle equations, circle angle properties, similarity/congruence and midpoint/tangent-chord theorems
Calculate the area of a rectilinear figure from its coordinates and justify the chosen decomposition
activities: Determine a circle from an original centre-radius constraint
Prove a statement in a constructed circle diagram and verify a coordinate example
evidence: Explains each proof step from stated properties
Completes the square to recover a circle centre and radius
units.bridge: S4 revisits proof through vectors and scaled areas/volumes.

units.title: Non-right triangles, radians and sectors
units.focus: Extend triangle reasoning to general angles and circular measure.
learning: Use sine/cosine rules, triangle area, bearings and elevation/depression in two- and three-dimensional problems
Convert radians/degrees and find arc, sector and segment measures
activities: Plan a triangulated survey from an invented set of distances and bearings
Compare sectors sharing a radius but different angles
Sketch the right triangles needed to find a diagonal length and an angle of elevation in a three-dimensional structure
evidence: Checks whether a sine-rule situation admits another triangle
Separates sector area from triangular area in a segment
Identifies the correct plane and triangle for each step of a three-dimensional trigonometry problem
units.bridge: Radian measure supports trigonometric graphs and calculus.

units.title: Trigonometric functions and identities
units.focus: Link circular motion, graphs and algebraic identities.
learning: Use six trigonometric functions, exact values and principal inverse values
Prove identities and solve equations on a specified interval using compound/double-angle and R-form expressions
activities: Construct a periodic model for an invented rotating marker
Compare algebraic and graphical solutions and locate every interval solution
evidence: Distinguishes a principal inverse value from the full interval solution set
Shows valid identity transformations and interprets amplitude and period
units.bridge: S4 differentiates these familiar functions; H2 later compares local approximations.

units.title: Graphs, modelling and synthesis
units.focus: Select a function family and test its implications.
learning: Sketch power, exponential and quadratic graphs and estimate a tangent gradient
Compare a model prediction with data and constraints
activities: Fit two plausible models to a small fictional data table
Write a model report that compares behaviour inside and beyond the observed range
evidence: Uses intercepts, asymptotic behaviour or turning points to justify a sketch
Identifies an unsupported extrapolation and explains the model limit
units.bridge: The estimated tangent gradient becomes a derivative in S4; begin by retrieving exact algebra and radians.

courses.title: Singapore mathematics — Secondary 4 · G3 + Additional Mathematics
courses.scopeNote: Selected advanced pathway combining G3 Mathematics and elective Additional Mathematics. Content is published for Secondary 3–4 together; this split is editorial and needs teaching time for both subjects.
prerequisites: Use advanced algebra, logarithms, radians and trigonometric identities
Explain circle/coordinate arguments and function graphs
outcomes: Use G3 sets, matrices, vectors, spread and combined probability
Differentiate and integrate the Additional Mathematics function families
Connect proof, calculus and data models with explicit assumptions
courses.nextStep: Continue to the selected H2 Mathematics route only after consolidating this elective foundation.
courses.yearBridge: Sets and matrices organise information, while vectors strengthen geometric arguments. Differentiation develops from local change into optimisation, and integration reverses it to describe accumulation; distribution and probability work then support the final model report.
courses.crossSubject: Write a mathematical report distinguishing observed data, a model assumption and a justified conclusion.
routines: Retrieve earlier number and algebra ideas each week and connect new work to diagrams and graphs.
Compare at least two representations or methods, then justify assumptions, restrictions and units.
Use technology to investigate and check; retain exact reasoning and explain what a numerical or graphical result can establish.

units.title: Sets, matrices and organised information
units.focus: Represent membership and repeated calculations precisely.
learning: Use set notation and Venn diagrams for two sets
Interpret and add, subtract or multiply appropriate matrices and scale a matrix
activities: Represent membership of two fictional clubs with sets
Use a quantity matrix and a price matrix to calculate several order costs
evidence: Distinguishes union, intersection and complement within a stated universal set
Explains the meaning and compatible dimensions of a matrix product
units.bridge: Sets later organise combined events; matrices demonstrate structured linear calculation.

units.title: Vectors, similarity and proof
units.focus: Use multiple representations of the same geometric relationship.
learning: Calculate with planar vectors, magnitudes and position vectors
Use area/volume scale factors, bisector constructions and geometric proof
activities: Prove a midpoint relationship with vectors and then geometrically
Compare scale models and construct a point constrained by angle or segment bisectors
evidence: Tracks vector direction and justifies a scalar multiple
Uses squared/cubed scale factors for area/volume rather than the length factor
units.bridge: H2 extends vector arguments to three dimensions and products.

units.title: Derivatives and function change
units.focus: Make the tangent gradient an algebraic function.
learning: Differentiate powers, trigonometric, exponential and logarithmic functions
Use product, quotient and chain rules and second-derivative notation
activities: Compare secant gradients approaching a point with the derivative value
Match original-function graphs to their derivative graphs
evidence: Selects a rule from the function structure
Explains a derivative value as a local rate with appropriate units
units.bridge: Derivative signs will support optimisation and motion analysis.

units.title: Tangents, rates and optimisation
units.focus: Connect a derivative calculation to the question being asked.
learning: Find tangents/normals, stationary points and increasing/decreasing intervals
Apply derivatives to connected rates and maximum/minimum problems
activities: Optimise an invented open container subject to a material constraint
Analyse a changing circular measurement using a supplied rate
evidence: Checks the nature and admissibility of stationary points
Uses the chain rule and units to interpret a connected rate
units.bridge: H2 extends these arguments to implicit and parametric curves.

units.title: Integration, area and motion
units.focus: Reverse differentiation and interpret signed accumulation.
learning: Integrate the syllabus power, trigonometric and exponential forms and simple linear composites
Evaluate definite integrals, areas and straight-line motion quantities
activities: Recover a position model from a velocity rule and an initial position
Find a region between a curve and a line, splitting at axis crossings when needed
evidence: Checks an antiderivative by differentiating
Distinguishes signed displacement from total distance and signed integral from area
units.bridge: H2 adds substitution, integration by parts and areas between two curves.

units.title: Spread and distribution comparisons
units.focus: Describe variation alongside a measure of centre.
learning: Interpret quartiles, percentiles, cumulative frequency and box plots
Calculate range, interquartile range and standard deviation for grouped/ungrouped data
activities: Compare fictional journey-time records with similar means
Construct a cumulative frequency graph and estimate percentile cutoffs
evidence: Identifies which measures use all values and which resist extreme values
Explains a comparison using both centre and spread
units.bridge: H2 probability models and sampling will quantify uncertainty about a population.

units.title: Combined probability
units.focus: Use a complete representation of multi-stage outcomes.
learning: Calculate combined-event probabilities using trees and possibility diagrams
Distinguish independent from mutually exclusive events and use addition/multiplication appropriately
activities: Compare draws with and without replacement from a small labelled set
Design two games with different event structures but the same win probability
evidence: Updates branch probabilities after an outcome when necessary
Explains why mutually exclusive events with positive probability are not independent
units.bridge: H2 extends this reasoning to conditional probability and combinatorial counting.

units.title: Connect calculus, models and evidence
units.focus: Integrate the two subjects while maintaining exact reasoning.
learning: Formulate and solve a multi-topic mathematical problem
Distinguish a proof, a numerical check and a model-based conclusion
activities: Compare two fictional production plans using rates, accumulated output and variability
Present a solution portfolio linking an algebraic, graphical and geometric method
evidence: States an assumption and checks domain, units and final feasibility
Explains one error corrected through a second representation
units.bridge: Begin H2 by checking algebra, functions, radians and calculus fluency; repair gaps before composite and inverse functions.

courses.title: Singapore mathematics — JC1 · selected H2 Mathematics pathway
courses.scopeNote: Selected H2 Mathematics pathway, year 1 of two. This JC year allocation is editorial, assumes Additional Mathematics and is not a universal grade expectation.
prerequisites: Complete the selected G3 and Additional Mathematics foundation
Use calculus, exact algebra, logarithms, trigonometry and planar vectors
outcomes: Analyse functions, sequences and Cartesian complex numbers
Use three-dimensional vectors and extend calculus
Count outcomes and calculate conditional probabilities
courses.nextStep: Continue H2 with series approximations, differential equations and statistical inference in JC2.
courses.yearBridge: Domain and graph reasoning supports equations, inequalities and sequences. Complex numbers and spatial vectors extend algebraic representation; implicit differentiation and advanced integration build on established functions, and counting provides the foundation for conditional probability.
courses.crossSubject: Translate an unfamiliar scientific or economic scenario into a model while stating the meanings and allowed values of every variable.
routines: Retrieve earlier number and algebra ideas each week and connect new work to diagrams and graphs.
Compare at least two representations or methods, then justify assumptions, restrictions and units.
Use technology to investigate and check; retain exact reasoning and explain what a numerical or graphical result can establish.

units.title: Functions, domains and inverses
units.focus: Separate a function rule from the domain on which it acts.
learning: Determine domain/range and whether an inverse or composite exists
Restrict a domain to obtain a one-to-one function and relate inverse graphs
activities: Compare several domains for the same quadratic rule
Build a composite process and trace an input through both stages
evidence: Checks that the inner output fits the outer domain
Justifies an inverse restriction and verifies the inverse relationship
units.bridge: Domain control matters for transformations, equations and modelling.

units.title: Graphs, transformations and inequalities
units.focus: Combine exact structure with reliable graphical investigation.
learning: Analyse conics, rational functions, asymptotes and simple parametric graphs
Use transformations, absolute values, reciprocal graphs and inequalities, including rational inequalities
Formulate and solve systems of linear equations with a graphing tool, then interpret the solution in context
activities: Predict transformed graphs before using software to check
Solve a constrained rational model with an exact sign diagram and graphical comparison
evidence: Labels forbidden inputs and distinguishes an asymptote from an intercept
States intervals and boundary inclusion correctly
units.bridge: These graph structures will guide calculus and solution checks throughout H2.

units.title: Sequences, series and recurrence
units.focus: Distinguish individual terms, partial sums and limiting behaviour.
learning: Use arithmetic/geometric terms and sums, including convergent infinite geometric series
Generate recurrence sequences and relate a term formula to partial sums
activities: Compare two fictional savings or depreciation plans
Investigate a recurrence numerically and test whether an apparent pattern is supported algebraically
evidence: States the convergence condition before an infinite sum
Distinguishes a sequence limit from convergence of its series
units.bridge: JC2 Maclaurin work uses series to approximate functions rather than only count terms.

units.title: Cartesian complex numbers
units.focus: Extend real arithmetic while preserving its algebraic structure.
learning: Calculate with complex numbers, modulus, argument and conjugates
Use conjugate polynomial roots and represent operations on an Argand diagram
activities: Locate roots of an original quadratic with no real roots
Show the geometric effects of addition, conjugation and multiplication by i
evidence: Rationalises a complex denominator using its conjugate
Relates algebraic operations to correct points and directions
units.bridge: Complex-number reasoning strengthens fluency and representation; polar/exponential form is outside this H2 outline.

units.title: Vectors, lines and planes in space
units.focus: Describe geometry through direction, position and products.
learning: Use scalar/vector products, unit vectors and three-dimensional line/plane equations
Find intersections, angles, perpendicular feet and point-to-line/plane distances
activities: Model a beam and surface in a three-dimensional coordinate frame
Compare intersecting, parallel and skew lines and justify the classification
evidence: Chooses a product for its geometric meaning
Checks an intersection in each original equation and reports a valid angle
units.bridge: These vector methods support later modelling; shortest distance between skew lines is outside this syllabus.

units.title: Extend differentiation
units.focus: Read local behaviour from derivatives and the defining relation.
learning: Differentiate simple implicit and parametric functions
Analyse stationary points, tangents, normals and connected rates
activities: Compare two ways of representing a curve near a point
Optimise a model subject to a physically meaningful domain
evidence: Explains the role of the first and second derivatives
Checks endpoint or domain constraints before claiming an optimum
units.bridge: JC2 uses repeated differentiation for Maclaurin approximations.

units.title: Integration techniques and accumulation
units.focus: Choose a transformation from the structure of an integrand.
learning: Use standard inverse-trigonometric forms, given substitutions and integration by parts
Evaluate definite integrals, areas between curves and volumes of revolution
activities: Sort integrands by a promising first transformation and justify the choice
Build a volume model from cross-sectional disks and compare with numerical integration
evidence: Verifies an antiderivative by differentiation
Uses intersections and sign changes to set correct limits
units.bridge: JC2 applies these tools to differential equations and reviews the limit-of-sums interpretation.

units.title: Counting and conditional probability
units.focus: Count cases without losing restrictions or the conditioning event.
learning: Use permutations/combinations, including line/circle arrangements with repetition or restrictions
Calculate conditional probabilities and test independence
activities: Count original seating arrangements by two different case decompositions
Compare a tree and two-way table for a fictional quality-screening process
evidence: Explains why outcomes are counted once
Uses the conditioning event as the denominator and interprets the result
units.bridge: JC2 packages outcomes into random-variable distributions, then studies samples from populations.

courses.title: Singapore mathematics — JC2 · selected H2 Mathematics pathway
courses.scopeNote: Selected H2 Mathematics pathway, year 2 of two. This JC year allocation is editorial, assumes Additional Mathematics and is not a universal grade expectation.
prerequisites: Use H2 functions, vectors, calculus and sequence methods
Count restricted outcomes and calculate conditional probabilities
outcomes: Use local series and separable differential-equation models
Analyse binomial/normal distributions, samples and mean tests
Evaluate regression models and integrated mathematical arguments
courses.nextStep: Move into further mathematics or applied study through explicit course prerequisites; this outline does not determine university placement.
courses.yearBridge: Maclaurin approximations and differential equations extend calculus models. Discrete and normal distributions support the transition from individual outcomes to sample means; hypothesis tests and regression then supply different kinds of evidence for the final integrated investigation.
courses.crossSubject: Read a quantitative research summary and separate a statistical association, a model prediction and a causal claim.
routines: Retrieve earlier number and algebra ideas each week and connect new work to diagrams and graphs.
Compare at least two representations or methods, then justify assumptions, restrictions and units.
Use technology to investigate and check; retain exact reasoning and explain what a numerical or graphical result can establish.

units.title: Maclaurin series and local approximation
units.focus: Use a polynomial to describe a function near zero.
learning: Use standard expansions and derive initial terms by repeated or implicit differentiation
State convergence restrictions and use small-angle approximations
activities: Compare several truncations with a graph of the original function
Build an approximation for a product or composition of standard series
evidence: Keeps terms to a justified order
States where the expansion or approximation is intended to work
units.bridge: Approximation becomes one tool for checking complicated model behaviour.

units.title: Integrals and differential-equation models
units.focus: Connect a rate law, its solution and an initial condition.
learning: Interpret a definite integral as a limit of sums and consolidate advanced integration
Formulate and solve separable differential equations, including a given substitution
activities: Derive an invented cooling or growth model from a stated rate assumption
Compare its predicted values with a small supplied data table
evidence: Uses an initial condition to determine the constant
Differentiates the solution to check the rate law and states its valid domain
units.bridge: The modelling cycle also guides decisions about probability distributions.

units.title: Discrete random variables and binomial models
units.focus: Move from listed outcomes to a distribution of numerical values.
learning: Construct a discrete probability distribution and find expectation/variance
Select and calculate with a binomial model and explain its assumptions
activities: Compare two original reward games using their distributions
Model repeated quality checks and discuss when a constant independent success probability is doubtful
evidence: Checks that probabilities sum to one
Distinguishes expected value from an outcome that must occur
units.bridge: Normal distributions describe continuous quantities; sampling later describes the behaviour of statistics.

units.title: Normal distributions and transformed variables
units.focus: Interpret probability as area for a continuous model.
learning: Calculate normal probabilities, quantiles and unknown parameters
Use expectations/variances of linear transformations and sums of independent variables
activities: Choose a tolerance interval in an invented manufacturing model
Compare one doubled measurement with the sum of two independent measurements
evidence: Explains the interval represented by a calculated probability
Uses different variance rules for scaling and independent addition
units.bridge: The normal model provides a distribution for sample means under suitable conditions.

units.title: Sampling and sample means
units.focus: Distinguish population variation from variation between samples.
learning: Explain simple random sampling and estimate population mean/variance
Use the sampling distribution of a mean and the Central Limit Theorem in suitable cases
activities: Simulate repeated samples from a fictional population
Compare how the spread of sample means changes with sample size
evidence: States what is random and what population quantity is fixed
Checks normal-population or sufficiently-large-sample conditions
units.bridge: A test for a population mean compares an observed sample statistic with this sampling model.

units.title: Tests for a population mean
units.focus: Frame a statistical conclusion in terms of evidence and assumptions.
learning: Set null/alternative hypotheses and conduct one- or two-tailed population-mean tests for a normal population with known variance, or for a sufficiently large sample from any population
Interpret significance level, critical region and p-value in context
activities: Assess an invented supplier claim from a supplied sample summary
Compare conclusions under two preselected significance levels
evidence: Chooses the tail from the research question before calculation
Avoids treating failure to reject as proof of the null or a p-value as its probability
Checks the normal-population/known-variance or large-sample condition before choosing a mean test; does not apply this procedure to a small sample with unknown population variance
units.bridge: Regression adds a second variable while retaining the need to check model assumptions.

units.title: Correlation, regression and transformations
units.focus: Use a fitted relationship for a defined predictive purpose.
learning: Interpret scatterplots and product-moment correlation
Use least-squares regression, choose the appropriate prediction direction, and linearise using square, reciprocal or logarithmic transformations
activities: Compare linear and transformed fits for a fictional response experiment
Evaluate an interpolation and an extrapolation from the same fitted model
evidence: Explains why association alone does not establish causation
States the model scale and reverses a transformation when interpreting predictions
units.bridge: The final synthesis weighs numerical fit alongside context and mathematical structure.

units.title: Integrated H2 investigation and transition
units.focus: Present a coherent argument linking several mathematical tools.
learning: Formulate and evaluate a multi-topic model with explicit assumptions
Select further study based on demonstrated prerequisite strengths and gaps
activities: Investigate an invented sensor system using a geometric setup, a change model and noisy measurements
Defend the result in a report and revise it after a peer challenges an assumption
evidence: Separates exact deductions, approximations and statistical evidence
Checks units, domains and conditions and names a concrete next learning need
units.bridge: Prepare for the chosen next course through its prerequisites, with targeted review of algebra, calculus, probability or proof as needed.
